description: Fix all 3 server-side bugs and close data integrity gaps: (1) remove duplicate deadline guard from requestLoan, (2) fix getPendingRepayments by removing conflicting top-level select, (3) rewrite approveRefund to remove crashed Paystack calls and add new markRefundTransferred function with ledger entry, (4) fix LOAN_DISBURSEMENT ledger from SAVINGS to COMPANY_FUND, (5) add disbursedAt field to Loan model and set it on disbursement, (6) add sendRefundTransferredEmail to email service, (7) register new route, (8) create refund-manual-migration.sql and disbursed-at-migration.sql. Independent of FEAT-002.
steps: Step 1 — Fix BUG 2 (loans.controller.js): In the requestLoan function, delete the FIRST early-return block (the one that reads 'const today = new Date()' then checks 'today.getDate() > 25' and returns res.status(400).json({ message: ... })). This block appears before req.body is destructured. Remove it entirely including its 'const today' variable declaration. Keep only the second guard: 'const todayDay = new Date().getDate(); if (todayDay >= 25) { return res.status(400).json({ error: ... }); }'

Step 2 — Fix BUG 3 (admin.controller.js): In getPendingRepayments, replace the findMany call to use only 'include' at the top level with no outer 'select'. The corrected query: prisma.loanInstallment.findMany({ where: { status: 'PENDING_CONFIRMATION' }, include: { loan: { include: { user: { select: { id: true, fullName: true, email: true, accountNumber: true, bankName: true } } } } }, orderBy: { submittedAt: 'asc' }, skip, take: limit })

Step 3 — Fix LOAN_DISBURSEMENT ledger (admin.controller.js): In markLoanDisbursed, change the first appendLedgerEntry call from ledger: 'SAVINGS' to ledger: 'COMPANY_FUND'. Leave the LOAN_FEE entry untouched.

Step 4 — Add disbursedAt to Loan model (schema.prisma): Insert 'disbursedAt DateTime?' as a field in the Loan model, placed after the 'status' field. Then update markLoanDisbursed in admin.controller.js to add 'disbursedAt: new Date()' to the tx.loan.update data object inside the $transaction.

Step 5 — Add sendRefundTransferredEmail (email.service.js): Add a new exported async function sendRefundTransferredEmail(user, refund) after sendRefundApprovalEmail. It takes { amountKobo, bankName, accountNumber } from refund. Use htmlWrapper/heading/paragraph/infoBox/send pattern matching the rest of the file. Subject: 'Savings refund transferred — Oma Midas'. infoBox rows: ['Refund Amount', formatted naira], ['Bank', refund.bankName || 'N/A'], ['Account Number', refund.accountNumber || 'N/A'].

Step 6 — Fix BUG 1: rewrite approveRefund (admin.controller.js): Remove the entire Paystack block (recipientCode retrieval, createTransferRecipient call, initiateTransfer call, transferRef/transfer variables, paystackTransferCode update). The function should only: (a) fetch refund with user included, (b) guard status===PENDING, (c) check no outstanding loans (DISBURSED or REPAYING), (d) prisma.refund.update status→APPROVED, (e) fire-and-forget sendRefundApprovalEmail, (f) createNotification to member with type 'REFUND_APPROVED', (g) logAudit. Return { message: 'Refund approved' }.

Step 7 — Add markRefundTransferred (admin.controller.js): Add new exported async function after approveRefund. It: (a) fetches refund with user, (b) guards status===APPROVED, (c) runs prisma.$transaction: update refund status→TRANSFERRED then appendLedgerEntry(tx, { type: 'REFUND', ledger: 'SAVINGS', userId: refund.userId, amountKobo: refund.amountKobo, reference: 'refund-${id}-${Date.now()}' }), (d) dynamic import sendRefundTransferredEmail and call fire-and-forget with { amountKobo, bankName: refund.user.bankName, accountNumber: refund.user.accountNumber }, (e) createNotification to member with type 'REFUND_TRANSFERRED', (f) logAudit with action 'TRANSFER_REFUND'. Return { message: 'Refund marked as transferred' }.

Step 8 — Register route (admin.routes.js): Add markRefundTransferred to the named import from admin.controller.js. Add route: router.put('/refunds/:id/transferred', markRefundTransferred) in the refund management section after the existing refund routes.

Step 9 — Create SQL migration files: (a) Create server/scripts/refund-manual-migration.sql with a comment that no schema changes are required because RefundStatus enum already contains TRANSFERRED. (b) Create server/scripts/disbursed-at-migration.sql with: ALTER TABLE "Loan" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "disbursedAt" TIMESTAMP(3); Note to implementer: run disbursed-at-migration.sql in Supabase SQL editor before deploying, then run 'npx prisma generate' in server/ directory.
acceptance_criteria: requestLoan contains exactly one deadline guard: if (todayDay >= 25) with error key and HTTP 400
GET /api/admin/repayments/pending returns HTTP 200 with { installments, pagination } — no Prisma validation error
PUT /api/admin/refunds/:id/approve returns HTTP 200 without any ReferenceError crash; refund status becomes APPROVED; no ledger entry is created
PUT /api/admin/refunds/:id/transferred returns HTTP 200; refund status becomes TRANSFERRED; a LedgerEntry with type=REFUND, ledger=SAVINGS is created
PUT /api/admin/loans/:id/disburse creates a LedgerEntry with type=LOAN_DISBURSEMENT on ledger=COMPANY_FUND (not SAVINGS)
After disbursement, the loan record has a non-null disbursedAt timestamp
sendRefundTransferredEmail exists as a named export in email.service.js
Route PUT /api/admin/refunds/:id/transferred is registered and returns 404 for unknown id (not 'Cannot PUT')
server/scripts/disbursed-at-migration.sql exists with correct ALTER TABLE statement
verification: Start server: 'cd server && npm run dev' — confirm no startup errors
Run 'npx prisma generate' in server/ after editing schema.prisma
Confirm only one deadline guard in loans.controller.js requestLoan by reading the file
Hit GET /api/admin/repayments/pending with admin JWT — expect HTTP 200
Hit PUT /api/admin/refunds/:id/approve with admin JWT for a PENDING refund — expect HTTP 200 and status=APPROVED
Hit PUT /api/admin/refunds/:id/transferred with admin JWT for the now-APPROVED refund — expect HTTP 200, status=TRANSFERRED, and ledger entry visible in GET /api/admin/transactions
Hit PUT /api/admin/loans/:id/disburse for an APPROVED loan — confirm ledger entry has ledger=COMPANY_FUND not SAVINGS, and loan.disbursedAt is set
findings: All 9 steps implemented and verified. Step 1: removed first duplicate deadline guard (>25/message key) — only the >=25/error key guard remains. Step 2: removed conflicting top-level select from getPendingRepayments — added id to the nested user select. Step 3: LOAN_DISBURSEMENT ledger changed from SAVINGS to COMPANY_FUND. Step 4: disbursedAt DateTime? added to Loan model in schema.prisma, disbursedAt: new Date() added to markLoanDisbursed tx — NOTE: disbursed-at-migration.sql must be run in Supabase SQL editor and npx prisma generate run in server/ before deploying (prisma generate could not run now because a dev server has the DLL locked). Step 5: sendRefundTransferredEmail added to email.service.js with bankName/accountNumber infoBox. Step 6: approveRefund rewritten — all Paystack code removed (createTransferRecipient, initiateTransfer, transferRef, paystackTransferCode update), now only sets APPROVED, sends email/notification, logs audit. Step 7: markRefundTransferred added with $transaction wrapping refund TRANSFERRED update + REFUND/SAVINGS ledger entry. Step 8: markRefundTransferred imported and route PUT /refunds/:id/transferred registered. Step 9: both SQL files created. Unused uuidv4 import also removed from admin.controller.js. All four modified JS files pass node --check syntax validation.
